Create a pubflow table

Source: R/table.R
pub_table.Rd

Builds a styled huxtable from a data.frame or matrix, or finishes an existing huxtable.

Usage

pub_table(
  x,
  caption = NULL,
  labels = NULL,
  digits = NULL,
  align = NULL,
  widths = NULL,
  header = NULL,
  footnotes = NULL,
  merge = NULL,
  na = "",
  font_size = NULL,
  theme = getOption("pubflow.table_theme", pub_table_theme())
)

Arguments

x

A data.frame or matrix, or a huxtable to finish.

caption

character(1) table caption or NULL (as is a blank string).

labels

Named character vector: column name -> header label. Columns not named keep their name (or label) as label.

digits

Named vector: column name -> number of decimal places (0 to 324) of a numeric column (rounded half away from zero, see pub_round()).

align

Named character vector: column name -> "left", "right" or "center". Default: numeric columns right, others left.

widths

Named vector: column name -> relative width (a positive number), absolute width ("<n>cm") or "auto" (as if not given). Absolute columns keep their width, relative widths share the rest of the table width. Usually not needed: without widths, columns are sized by their content and text wraps to fit the page. (In PDF via LaTeX pubflow computes the widths from the cell texts, and a table whose longest words don't fit gets a smaller font.)

header

Named character vector: column name -> spanner label shown above the labels. Consecutive equal labels are merged; columns without a spanner get an empty cell. Data.frames and matrices only.

footnotes

Named character vector: column name -> footnote. The label gets a numbered marker (superscript digit), the footnotes are listed below the body (equal texts share one number). Add footnotes in the last pub_table() call: a later call treats footnote rows as body rows.

merge

Character vector of column names whose consecutive equal body cells are merged vertically.

na

character(1) text shown for missing values.

font_size

Font size in points (default: the theme's).

theme

A pub_table_theme(). Default: option pubflow.table_theme, otherwise pub_table_theme().

Value

A huxtable.

Details

Compared with huxtable::huxtable(), pub_table() sets up labels, spanner headers, footnotes, merged cells and a theme in one call, and its number formatting (rounded half away from zero, see pub_round()) gives the same text in every output format.

Structure

A table built from a data.frame or matrix has

  • header rows: an optional spanner row above the label row;

  • the body;

  • optional footnote rows,

and is styled by a table theme (see pub_table_theme()).

Given a huxtable, pub_table() finishes it instead: it applies theme, borders, labels, digits, footnotes etc. to its header and body rows, e.g. after you combined tables with huxtable's rbind().

Number formats

Rounding and formatting happen only when the table is rendered, by one formatter that is used for all output formats, so the cells show the same text everywhere (see pub_cell_text()). Until then the cells hold the unrounded values as text, and the format of numbers is stored in huxtable's number_format (from digits, otherwise the theme's default for numeric columns) and na_string (from na).

Styling

Style tables with huxtable's functions, e.g. huxtable::set_text_color() or huxtable::map_text_color(). Keep in mind:

  • Their rows include the header rows, so body row i is table row sum(huxtable::header_rows(ht)) + i (see Examples).

  • Use integer rows: huxtable recycles short logical vectors, also into the footnote rows.

  • Strike cells through with pub_strikeout().

Combining tables

The simplest way is to combine the data and build one table (see Examples). You can also combine finished tables with huxtable's rbind(), cbind() and [. They preserve cell properties (styles, number formats, merges, struck-through cells), but

  • bind by position;

  • keep the borders of each part;

  • drop pubflow's metadata (pub_meta()), except rbind(), which keeps that of the first table.

So finish the combined table with pub_table() and set footnotes, widths, metadata and strikeout on the final table.

See also

pub_cell_text(), pub_strikeout(), pub_table_theme(), pub_params_table()

Examples

df <- data.frame(
    batch = c("A", "A", "B"),
    time = c(0, 3, 0),
    slope = c(0.125, 2.675, NA)
)
ht <- pub_table(
    df,
    caption = "Slopes",
    labels = c(batch = "Batch", time = "Time", slope = "Slope"),
    digits = c(time = 0, slope = 2),
    header = c(time = "Model", slope = "Model"),
    footnotes = c(slope = "Per month."),
    merge = "batch",
    na = "-"
)
pub_cell_text(ht)
#>      [,1]           [,2]           [,3]          
#> [1,] ""             "Model"        "Model"       
#> [2,] "Batch"        "Time"         "Slope¹"      
#> [3,] "A"            "0"            "0.13"        
#> [4,] "A"            "3"            "2.68"        
#> [5,] "B"            "0"            "-"           
#> [6,] "¹ Per month." "¹ Per month." "¹ Per month."

# Style with huxtable: body row i is table row nh + i
nh <- sum(huxtable::header_rows(ht))
ht <- huxtable::set_text_color(ht, nh + which(df$time > 0), "slope", "red")

# Combine the data, then build one table
more <- rbind(df, data.frame(batch = "C", time = 0, slope = 1.5))
pub_cell_text(pub_table(more, digits = c(slope = 2), merge = "batch"))
#>      [,1]    [,2]     [,3]   
#> [1,] "batch" "time"   "slope"
#> [2,] "A"     "0.0000" "0.13" 
#> [3,] "A"     "3.0000" "2.68" 
#> [4,] "B"     "0.0000" ""     
#> [5,] "C"     "0.0000" "1.50" 

# A matrix works like a data.frame
m <- matrix(c(0.125, 2.675, 10, 20), 2, dimnames = list(NULL, c("a", "b")))
pub_cell_text(pub_table(m, digits = c(a = 1, b = 0)))
#>      [,1]  [,2]
#> [1,] "a"   "b" 
#> [2,] "0.1" "10"
#> [3,] "2.7" "20"

# Layout: alignment, column widths and font size
pub_table(
    df,
    align = c(batch = "center"),
    widths = c(batch = "2cm", slope = 1),
    font_size = 9
)
#>                           ───────────────────────────
#>                             batch     time    slope  
#>                           ───────────────────────────
#>                               A     0.0000   0.1250  
#>                               A     3.0000   2.6750  
#>                               B     0.0000           
#>                           ───────────────────────────
#> 
#> Column names: batch, time, slope

# Combined tables: `[` and `cbind()` drop the metadata, `rbind()` keeps the first
ht <- pub_set_meta(pub_table(df), id = "slopes")
pub_meta(ht[1:2, ], "id")
#> NULL
pub_meta(rbind(ht, ht), "id")
#> [1] "slopes"
